new.n: Jack Hession's re-hidden gold, farm timber southwest of Humboldt
new.pl: Timber at the Indian Creek mouth on the neighbouring farm, NW sec. 24 T91N R29W, Corinth Township; the 1896 Hession homestead was about 1 km NW in the SE quarter of sec. 14
new.v: Tin can of gold coins and bills ($1,500-3,000 reputed)
new.st: About 1875 Mrs. Hession and her sons farmed southwest of Humboldt. Jack buried every cent he got. His brothers once caught him digging up a tin can of gold coins and bills ($800-1,000) in the yard; that night he carried it down the road into the timber on a neighbouring farm and came back without it, and he did the same for years. When he was committed to the state hospital in 1915, his brother said Jack had buried $2,500-3,000 and had re-hidden one found cache of about $1,500 'together with better than $1,000 more'. It was still unfound in 1935.
new.t: Two separate accounts (1915 and 1935) and a placed spot. Search the woodlot at the Indian Creek mouth; the Hession homestead yard (SE¼ sec. 14) is a second spot. Private: ask permission.
